key_insight: Laser remelting densified detonation-sprayed NiCrFeBSiC coatings, increasing hardness and adhesion while reducing specific wear rate by 49.5%.
engineering_relevance: This combined treatment could improve wear-resistant protective coatings on stainless-steel components in mechanical and power engineering.
method: Detonation-spray NiCrFeBSiC onto AISI 321 stainless steel, then laser-remelt.
Compare microstructure, composition, and phases using SEM, EDS, and XRD.
Evaluate indentation properties, adhesion, friction, wear, and electrochemical corrosion.
evidence_signal: Before–after tests showed porosity decreasing from 0.306% to 0.15%, hardness increasing from 1049.1 to 1206.1 HV, and friction coefficient decreasing from 0.535 to 0.409.
watch_item: Corrosion current density decreased by only approximately 3%; the abstract does not establish long-term service durability.
paper_title: Effect of Laser Remelting on the Microstructure, Mechanical and Tribological Properties of Detonation-Sprayed NiCrFeBSiC Coatings for Mechanical Engineering Applications
